examples.label: Prepend the current directory to PATH
Plant a malicious 'ls' the root program will call

notes: For real escalation the payload should do something useful (copy bash to /tmp and setuid, add sudoers line, etc.) rather than echo.

recommended.note: Needs a SUID/root program that calls a binary by relative name.

name: Path Abuse - Hijack a Relative Binary Call
description: If a privileged script/binary calls another command by name (not full path), prepend a writable dir to PATH and drop a malicious binary with that name so it runs instead.

steps.label: 1. Inspect and extend PATH
steps.command:
echo $PATH
env | grep PATH
PATH=.:${PATH}
export PATH
echo $PATH

steps.label: 2. Plant malicious replacement (e.g. ls)
steps.command:
touch ls
echo 'echo "PATH ABUSE!!"' > ls
chmod +x ls

defense.why_it_works: If . (current directory) or a user-controlled directory appears early in $PATH, commands without full paths are resolved from the attacker's directory first. When a privileged script (cron, sudo, SUID) runs a command by name only (e.g., 'ls' or 'id'), the attacker's malicious binary in their controlled PATH entry is executed instead of the system binary.
defense.prerequisites: A PATH entry controlled by the attacker (current dir in PATH, writable directory before /usr/bin). A privileged script that calls commands without full absolute paths.
defense.impact: Code execution as the privileged user running the script (root). Can be leveraged to add sudoers entries, create SUID shells, or execute reverse shells as root.
defense.detection: Unexpected binary names in home directory or /tmp matching system command names. Unusual process execution where 'ls' or 'id' runs from an unexpected path. Auditd: execve of command from non-standard path.
defense.artifacts: Auditd: execve('/home/user/ls') called by root cron | Process audit: command executed from unexpected directory
defense.prevention: Always use absolute paths in scripts and cron jobs (/usr/bin/ls, /bin/id). Never include . or user-writable directories in root's PATH. Audit PATH in cron jobs and sudo scripts. Use 'secure_path' in /etc/sudoers to override user PATH for sudo commands.
defense.misconfiguration: Root-executed script or cron job calls commands without absolute paths. Root's PATH or the script's runtime PATH includes . (current directory) or user-controlled directories before /usr/bin.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Insecure script (no absolute paths)
#!/bin/bash
backup_files=$(ls -la /backup/)
id

# PATH with . first (extremely dangerous)
PATH=.:$PATH
defense.secure_config:
# Always use absolute paths in privileged scripts
#!/bin/bash
backup_files=$(/bin/ls -la /backup/)
/usr/bin/id

# /etc/sudoers -- enforce secure PATH
Defaults secure_path="/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"

# Never set PATH=.:$PATH for root
defense.evasion: Create malicious binary with the same name as a command used in the target script. Ensure it's in a directory that appears before /usr/bin in PATH.
